units.title: Fuel and oil: count before the boat
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi, before the next supply run could you count what's left of:
- saw fuel (drums and cans)
- bar and chain oil
- generator diesel
The charter can carry six drums at most. I'd rather send what you need than what the list says, as the list was written before the storm cost us three days. A rough number by tomorrow lunchtime is fine. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: First aid kit: monthly check
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, this is the routine monthly reminder for the site first aid kit. Please check the eye wash bottles, the large dressings and the burn gel against the card in the lid, and tick the date. If anything is short, add it to the supply list and I'll send it on the boat. It isn't urgent, but the insurers do ask to see the card. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Five ways to keep your camp cosy this week!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Evenings drawing in? Here are our top five ways to keep your camp cosy: 1. a draught strip on the door, 2. a wool blanket over the mattress, not under, 3. a thermos filled before dark, 4. socks drying on a line, never on the stove, 5. a good lantern, lit early! Our Glowmaster lanterns are 20% off until the weekend.

units.title: Forecast: dry, sunny, light winds
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. A frosty start inland, minus 3 C at Brackwater, with icy patches on untreated roads. Dry with long sunny spells. Wind northwesterly 2 to 3. Sea state slight, swell decreasing. Visibility very good. Maximum 8 C. Tonight: clear and calm at first, cloud thickening from the south after midnight with patchy mist near coasts.

units.title: Busy afternoon sailings
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. While night crossings are reduced, our 17:30 and 20:15 departures from Port Ammet are expected to be very busy. Foot passengers are advised to arrive 20 minutes before departure. Vehicle bookings on the 20:15 are now full for the next five days. An extra 18:45 foot-passenger sailing to Lisle and Gilliver will run from tomorrow, subject to crew availability.

units.title: Route deviation at Lisle Spit
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. Because the Lisle Spit buoy is off station, vessels will take the wider southern approach into Lisle until it is re-laid. This adds about six minutes to crossings calling at Lisle. Connections at Port Ammet may be tight. We will update customers when normal routeing resumes.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. All customers affected by the storm have now been reconnected. Engineers will continue to patrol lines in the Brackwater and Tollinby areas over the coming days to check for damage that may not yet have caused a fault. If your lights are flickering or dimming, please report it rather than waiting for it to fail.

units.title: Planned work: Tollinby Market Street
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Planned maintenance on the Tollinby Market Street cable will require a supply interruption to 46 properties between 09:00 and 13:00 in four days' time. Affected customers will receive a card through the door. This work was scheduled before the storm and is not related to it.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. The lower Tollinby road at the Mill Bridge has reopened under temporary traffic lights after the fallen beech was cleared. The slipped verge will be repaired over the next two weeks; expect delays. The Brackwater ridge road reopened last night. Thank you to residents who helped clear branches from the ridge road.

units.title: Gilliver sea wall inspection
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Engineers will inspect the Gilliver sea wall today after storm overtopping. The harbour road will remain single-lane at the wall until the inspection is complete and stones have been cleared. Residents of the Front Row cottages are asked to report any water in cellars to the council's flooding line.

units.title: Brackwater reservoir: overflow
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council, on behalf of the water authority. The Brackwater reservoir overflow channel is running for the first time since the winter before last. This is normal and the dam is safe. Tap water is not affected. The spillway viewpoint is closed. Please keep children and dogs away from the channel and the outflow at the dam foot.

units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. Further to the earlier notice, the buoy tender will re-lay the Lisle Spit east cardinal tomorrow morning on the first of the flood. Until then, the buoy should be treated as unreliable. Floating debris continues to be reported in the Gilliver channel, including a small green rowing boat, last seen drifting east of the harbour mouth.

units.author: met
units.text: Evening forecast, 18:00 ST. Clear for a time, then cloud thickening from the south after midnight with patchy mist and dew near coasts, particularly around Gilliver and Lisle. Light southerly winds. Minimum 3 C. Tomorrow: cloudy and mild, dry. High water at Gilliver 05:31 and 17:56.

units.title: Forgotten 1950s plan for a light on Kittering Holm resurfaces
units.author: courier
units.text: A plan to build an unattended lighthouse relay on Kittering Holm, quietly dropped seventy years ago, has resurfaced as interest grows in the island's future. The proposal, made by the Lights Board in 1953, would have carried the Carrow Point signal to Lisle and the southern channel from a tower on the Holm's northern knoll.

units.author: courier
units.text: The survey, a copy of which is held by the Marrow Sound History Society, found the site suitable. It recommended against building, citing 'reasons of staffing'. The Courier reported the plan's abandonment in a single paragraph in the winter of 1954, and it does not appear to have been discussed again.

units.author: courier
units.text: A planning consultant who found the original consultation in the council archive said there was 'nothing sinister' in it. 'The Board was closing stations all over the country at the time,' she said. 'It's an interesting footnote. It does not tell you anything about what anyone wants to do with the island now.'

units.author: courier
units.text: One detail has attracted attention online: the survey notes that the party asked on its third day to be taken off the island before dusk each evening rather than camp there as planned. A Gilliver man whose family supplied the boatmen said the arrangement was common sense. 'It was November. They had beds in the village. Wouldn't you?'

units.author: courier
units.text: Ardent Vale Holdings, which bought the Holm through an intermediary eighteen months ago, did not respond to questions about whether it was aware of the survey. Grieve Land Services, which is clearing the island's trees under a 30-day contract, said it 'does not comment on the client's plans'.

units.title: Shift workers stranded by night ferry cuts
units.author: courier
units.text: Hospital and care staff who live on Lisle and in Gilliver say the loss of the late ferry has left them choosing between leaving work early and sleeping in Port Ammet. Port Ammet General said it was aware of the problem and was allowing affected staff to swap onto earlier shifts where it could.

units.author: courier
units.text: One healthcare assistant from Gilliver said she had spent the first night of the new timetable on a friend's sofa. 'I don't mind once,' she said. 'I mind not knowing for how long.' A care home on Lisle has put two camp beds in its staff room for night workers who cannot get back across.

units.author: courier
units.text: The council's transport lead said the district had asked Sound Lines to consider an extra early-evening sailing and had approached a coach firm about a late road link to Gilliver. The road journey is around fifty minutes, against twenty-five by ferry, and does not help Lisle, which has no road connection.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines said it would introduce an additional 18:45 foot-passenger sailing from tomorrow, crew permitting. It repeated that the night timetable change was temporary but declined to give an end date for its welfare review.

units.title: Sound Lines: welfare review will take 'weeks, not months'
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Sound Lines has told Sound FM that its review of night crew welfare will take 'weeks, not months'. A spokesperson said the company wanted to look at rest periods, rostering and what support was available to crew on night services, and that the storm had 'brought some of those questions forward'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Asked directly whether any crew member had reported feeling unsafe on night services, the spokesperson said the company 'would not discuss individual concerns raised in confidence'. The seafarers' branch said its members had raised a number of issues, which it described as 'a mixture of the ordinary and the less ordinary'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The branch would not explain what it meant by 'less ordinary'. Its secretary said: 'People work nights on the water for years and see all sorts. When enough of them say they're tired, you listen. That's all this is.'

units.title: Live: frosty roads after the storm
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:00. A hard frost inland this morning, minus three at Brackwater according to the Met Office and minus four according to a listener's car. Gritters went out overnight on the main routes, but the lanes around the reservoir are icy and still carrying storm debris. Take it slowly.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:35. A van has slid into the verge on the Brackwater ridge road near Holly Lane. Nobody hurt, says the driver, who rang us from the cab while waiting for a tow and asked us to tell his boss he will be late. Consider it done, Mick.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:05. The Mill Bridge on the lower Tollinby road is open again under temporary lights. A listener reports the queue is already back to the garage. Another listener reports the temporary lights at the Brackwater junction are still stuck on red, which we understand is not news.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 09:10. The sun is up properly now and the frost is going from the coast roads. School buses are running to time. That's it from the travel desk for this morning. Clear skies, light winds, and for once nothing falling over.

units.title: Night buses back to full timetable after storm
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven's night bus network returned to its full timetable last night after three days of storm cuts. The city's transport operator said fallen trees on the ring road and flooding at the Docks underpass had forced it to withdraw four routes, stranding late-shift workers across the city.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The operator thanked depot staff, including cleaners and fitters, who it said had kept the fleet ready through the storm. A depot worker said the yard had been 'full of buses with nowhere to go' for three nights, all of them parked with interior lights left on for the cleaners.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Passengers are reminded that the N4 to the Dellow and Harker estates now runs every 30 minutes rather than every 20 after midnight, a change introduced before the storm that the operator says will be reviewed in the new year.

units.title: City to review private bin contracts at tower blocks
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven city council will review how privately managed tower blocks arrange their waste collections after complaints from tenants at several estates, including Dellow Court, of missed and erratic pickups. Blocks owned by private landlords can use their own contractors rather than the council's rounds.

units.author: weypost
units.text: One Dellow Court tenant, a retired bus driver, told the Post he had kept a written log of every collection since the summer and had sent copies to the council and to the building's managing agent. 'The lorry came at five in the morning and then not for nine days,' he said. 'I have it written down.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates, which manages Dellow Court, said its waste contract was 'being kept under review'. The council expects to report to its environment committee early next year.

units.title: Storm-felled timber floods regional market
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Merchants across the Marrow Sound expect a glut of storm-felled softwood and broadleaf over the coming weeks as estates clear windblown trees. Early estimates from Brackwater and Tollinby suggest several thousand tonnes came down, much of it shallow-rooted spruce on the ridge plantations.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Windblown timber is slower and more dangerous to process than standing trees, with root plates that can swing back upright when the trunk is cut free and stems held under tension. Contractors with storm-work experience are in demand, and day rates for experienced fellers have risen accordingly.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: For merchants, the risk is a short-term fall in prices for mixed softwood. Buyers already committed to large volumes, including logs expected from the Kittering Holm clearance, may find the market less generous than it looked a month ago.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The industry's safety body has reminded members that storm work should be carried out by ticketed operators only, and that homeowners should not attempt to cut fallen trees under tension themselves. 'Every storm, somebody's uncle borrows a saw,' its chair said.

units.title: Engineers inspect Gilliver sea wall after overtopping
units.author: courier
units.text: Council engineers spent the day examining the Gilliver sea wall after waves topped it on two high tides during the storm. Early findings suggest the wall itself is sound but that several coping stones were lifted, and that the drain behind the Front Row cottages was overwhelmed.

units.author: courier
units.text: Residents of Front Row said water came under two doors on the second night. One retired resident, who has lived on the front for most of her life, said she had moved her rugs upstairs and kept her lamp lit in the window as usual. 'The sea comes in,' she said. 'You keep the house going.'

units.author: courier
units.text: The harbour road will stay single-lane at the wall until the coping stones are reset, expected later this week. The council said it would also look again at a long-delayed scheme to raise the wall by half a metre, first proposed after a storm a decade ago.

units.title: Letters: islands, ferries and rakes
units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, your report on the Kittering Holm clearance asks what the owners intend. May I ask instead why anyone needs to know? It is private land, lawfully bought, and the trees are being felled with permission. We would not ask a farmer to explain his plans for a field. Name and address supplied, Tollinby.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, the night ferry is not a luxury. My daughter is a nurse who finishes at ten. Sound Lines may review the welfare of its crew as long as it likes, but whose welfare is served by a young woman sleeping in her car at the terminal? I would be grateful for an answer from the company. Name and address supplied, Lisle.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, during the storm a man on my lane attempted to move a fallen power cable with a garden rake. I write not to shame him, he knows who he is, but to say that the linemen who came out at two in the morning were patient, courteous and very wet. Thank you to them. Name and address supplied, Brackwater.

units.title: Pay statement available (ref GLS-PS-1703)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: This is an automated message. A pay statement for the period ending yesterday is available. Contract: KH-30. Day rate: $300 per worker per day. Tree rate: $100 per tree as recorded by the client count. Deductions: none recorded. Please retain this statement for your records. Queries to Operations. Do not reply to this address.

units.title: Notice: outstanding crew wages (ref GLS-AR-1703)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: This is an automated reminder. The register for contract KH-30 shows crew wages outstanding at the end of the last working day. Status: OUTSTANDING. Wages should be settled at the site terminal. This notice will repeat daily until the balance is cleared. Queries to Operations. This mailbox is not monitored.

units.title: Did you know? Working away may affect your cover
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Good morning! Did you know that some home and personal policies may not cover belongings kept at remote work sites, temporary accommodation or 'locations not accessible by road'? With more of our customers working away, it's worth checking. Our Away From Home add-on gives you peace of mind wherever the job takes you. Exclusions apply; see policy wording section 7(c).

units.title: Storm damage: anything to claim?
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi, the insurers have asked all sites to list any storm damage by the end of the week. A short list is fine:
- what was damaged or lost
- roughly when
- whether work stopped because of it
No photographs needed unless it's over $500. If nothing was damaged, a one-line 'nil' in the site log is enough, I can read it from there. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Numbers for the client
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, just checking where we are on numbers. The client has asked for a midpoint figure, which I've said I'll take from the site count rather than guess. They are still very hands-off, they just like to see a number. I know the storm cost days. Nobody expects miracles, only a figure. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi again. I've looked at the site count. I'll be honest with you: it's well short of where head office hoped to be by now, and the storm only explains part of it. I'm not asking for anything unreasonable, just a plan for the next fortnight I can put in front of them. Let's not let it slide further. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Crew numbers
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I've seen that the crew is one short. I'm sorry; it's never pleasant. Head office can't send anyone across before the next boat at the earliest, and frankly nobody local is queuing up for an island job at the moment. Please make sure the remaining crew know the day rate continues and that nobody is expected to work alone in the far stands. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, following up on the Courier. There's another piece today, about an old lighthouse survey of the Holm. Nothing to do with us, but it keeps the island in the paper. If anyone from a newspaper, radio or the forums contacts you, please don't reply, and do let me know. Head office are a little sensitive at the moment. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Rest and lights
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, one small thing. Sound Lines are reviewing night crew rest, and head office have asked all site leads to remind crews about proper rest after a storm week. Practically: nobody working after dark, the usual camp lights on at dusk, and early nights. I know you do this already. I'm asked to put it in writing. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: why did the lumberjack get the sack
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: he took too many leaves. I'm here all week, unfortunately, the road job's been extended. foreman fell in a ditch today, in front of the client, the ditch he told us not to dig. best day of the contract. hope the island's treating you better than the storm did. H

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: PS don't take the Corran thing as gospel, chief. I've had a drink since and I still mean it, but I don't want you lying awake on my account. you've got a good crew, from what I hear. keep them fed and keep them in at night and you'll be fine. that's all it ever was. H

units.title: Kittering Holm: the 1953 survey
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text:
Hello. You may have seen our piece today about the 1953 lighthouse survey. One line in it, about the survey party leaving before dusk, has caused more letters than the rest put together. I've no wish to make something of it. But I wondered:
1. Does your crew stay on the island overnight?
2. Do you have a boat on hand in the evenings?
As always, nothing would be attributed. I've asked Grieve too. Best, Nell

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: A short follow-up, sorry. Sound Lines told a colleague today that some crew had raised 'less ordinary' concerns about night crossings. I'm not asking you about Sound Lines. I'm only noting that your camp is the one place on that stretch of water that is lit every night. If anything unusual has been seen from the island side, I would like to know. Nell

units.title: hospital bag (a saga)
units.author: sam
units.text: packed Mum's hospital bag tonight, or rather Mum packed it and I unpacked the three hardback novels and the good teapot. she says the hospital tea is 'a disgrace to the leaf'. she's nervous, you can tell because she's cleaned the oven. Bea's tree costume is green bin liners and cardboard, she wants to know if you'll be back for the play. I said probably not but that you'd want photos. anyway. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: can't sleep, so here's a pointless email. the dog's on my feet. I keep reading the stuff about the ferries and the old lighthouse thing on the island and then telling myself it's the Courier, they made a story out of a bin lorry this week. are you sleeping? you never sleep before a big day either. ok. going to try again. S x

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Sorry, I forgot to say yesterday, and I know it's silly. When he was little Tomas used to sleep better with a light on in the hall. If there's a light on at night where you are, that's probably why he'd sleep at all. I'm not asking you to do anything. I just wanted someone there to know. Ana

units.title: Is Tomas all right?
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: I'm sorry to ask this. Someone at work said they'd heard one of the crew had come back from the island. I don't know if it's true and I don't know who. Please, if you can, tell me Tomas is all right. If it was him, he hasn't rung me, and he always rings me. Ana

units.title: Brightest in the Sound: lantern week starts now
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: It's lantern week at Camp Supply! Our Glowmaster 800 throws a warm, even light across a whole camp yard, runs nine hours on a charge and shrugs off rain. Pair it with a hanging hook and a spare battery and save 15%. Customers say it's 'like having the porch light on'. Order by Friday for next-boat delivery to remote sites. Stay bright!

units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.title: Lights Board survey of Kittering Holm (1953), part 2: costs
units.text: 5. Estimate of costs. Clearance of tower strip, 40 m by 120 m, by contract: 310 pounds. Tower and lantern, steel, 9 m: 1,840 pounds. Keeper's hut and store: 620 pounds. Landing stage, timber: 450 pounds. Boat hire during survey, additional to estimate owing to daily return: 38 pounds 10 shillings. Annual cost of attendance by visiting keeper from Carrow Point: see section 6.

units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 5a. Note on clearance. The contractor's estimate assumes daylight working only, as the party's own experience suggests is advisable on the Holm in the winter months. A contractor intending to camp on the island should be asked to price accordingly. The undersigned would not recommend that the clearance strip be extended beyond what the tower requires.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr 9th. Fog off the water all day, could not see the Gilliver side. Felled 22 only. Mr Coad's rule made stricter: no man to cross the yard after the lamps without another. Pascoe laughed at it and went out alone to the privy and came in again very quick and laughed no more. Tally 2,301. Paid out 4 pounds 6s.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr 11th. Boat came. Hosking and the two Rowe brothers took it back across, paid off at their own asking, not dismissed. Roster 14 men. Wind E, bitter. The men have taken to keeping a lamp burning in each hut window all night, which costs oil, and Mr Coad allows it. Felled 30.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Middle watch. 00:00 wind S 2, light mist over the water, vis. 2 miles. 00:45 lamp trimmed. 01:20 fog signal not required. 02:30 mist thickening, vis. 1 mile. Remarks: one walker on the shore road, standing below the light at the edge of the beam's dip. Hailed. Did not answer. Lost to view when the beam came round. 04:00 relieved.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Morning watch, same date. 06:15 lamp extinguished, curtains drawn. 07:00 walked the shore road to the village for the post. No footprints in the frost on the verge where I had seen the walker, though the verge is soft. Remarks: possibly the mist misled me as to the distance. Wind S 2, vis. good.

units.title: Field notebook, Miss H. Arnell, 1923: the Holm survey
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Day 3 on the Holm. Browse excellent: bramble, ivy, young holly all untouched to head height. [Sketch: holly sapling, unbitten.] No slots, no droppings, no lying-up places, no fraying on any stem. On the mainland at Brackwater one cannot walk fifty yards without deer sign. Either the Holm has never had deer, or they do not care for it. The boatman says the second and will not explain.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Day 4. Birds: Turdus silvanus common in the understorey, wrens everywhere, a single owl, Strix holmensis I think, though I heard it only. Noted that birdsong stops entirely about half an hour before dusk, earlier than on Lisle. The boatman arrives at four sharp to take me off and will not wait past half past, which is tiresome when the light is good.

units.title: 1911: 'Gilliver Notes', two consecutive weeks
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: From our Gilliver Correspondent. It is whispered along the harbour, and I give it as a whisper only, that the low building on the Holm's eastern shore was once a quarantine station for sailors brought in sick from foreign ports, and that some lie buried there. Certainly the older folk will not land on that side. Your correspondent offers it to the reader for what it is worth, which may be little.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: From our Gilliver Correspondent, a week later. I am obliged to several correspondents, and to one very firm lady of the harbour, for informing me that the building on the Holm was a fish-curing house, worked by Gilliver families within living memory, and that no sick sailor ever set foot in it. Your correspondent withdraws the whisper, and begs pardon of the curing families.

units.title: Diary of Amos Rendle, fisherman, 1930s: extracts
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 3. Wind NE, cold. Lifted 40 pots, 9 lobster, prices fair. Father says the curing house on the Holm is to be pulled down, it is not used since the war. I worked there as a boy salting herring with my aunt. Never a sick man was sent there whatever they say in Port Ammet. Mother lit the lamp at five.

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 9. Lost a fleet of pots off the Holm north end, the rope chafed through on the rocks. Could see the floats at dusk close in under the trees but did not go in for them. Tom said leave them till morning, and in the morning they was gone. Bought new rope, 3s 4d. Dear.

units.title: Talk: Holm timber camp, abandonment (dispute)
units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. The article states the 1894-95 camp was abandoned 'for reasons unknown'. I propose the simpler explanation: a pay dispute. The clerk's diary records men 'paid off at their own asking' in December, falling tallies and rising oil costs. Men leaving a winter camp over money is the commonest story in the trade. I'd ask Marsh to stop restoring 'reasons unknown' until someone has looked at the wage ledger. Pell.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-2233. Brackwater reservoir, spillway running, recorded from the dam road. Handheld recorder, 18 min. Broadband water noise, steady; occasional percussive events at the outflow pipe, attributed by the recordist to air in the pipe. LB-2234. Gilliver harbour, inner basin, morning after storm. Hydrophone, 26 min. Hull slap, mooring chains, a diesel at idle. Curator's note: the diesel is identified as the harbourmaster's tender.
